statements.text: MGUS is common, usually asymptomatic, and not cancer, but it can progress to myeloma or related lymphoplasmacytic malignancy.
Myeloma is often difficult to identify early because symptoms can be vague; do not miss CRAB features or malignant spinal cord compression.

history.text: Ask about unexplained bony back pain or other bone pain, unexplained fracture, fatigue, recurrent infection, polyuria, polydipsia, confusion, pruritus without rash, neuropathy, and weight loss.

examination.text: Check hydration, pallor, bone tenderness, neurological symptoms/signs, gait, power, sensation, reflexes, and bladder or bowel disturbance when back pain is present.

tests.text: Initial tests: FBC, U&E/eGFR, calcium, ESR or plasma viscosity, LFT, serum immunoglobulins, serum protein electrophoresis, and sFLC; request urine Bence Jones protein if sFLC is not available.
If serum protein electrophoresis is abnormal, serum immunofixation is needed to confirm paraprotein.
Do not rely on one negative paraprotein, light-chain, or urine test alone to exclude myeloma if symptoms remain concerning.

red_flags.text: Suspected myeloma with malignant spinal cord compression symptoms/signs or acute kidney injury requires same-day hospital assessment.
Myeloma-suggestive tests plus any CRAB feature require urgent suspicion of cancer referral.

statements.text: Treat MGUS as a monitoring diagnosis, not a treatment diagnosis. Give safety-net advice to report new bone pain, fractures, fatigue, recurrent infections, neuropathy, weight loss, polyuria/polydipsia, or symptoms of anaemia.

For newly identified low-risk MGUS, repeat FBC, U&E/eGFR, calcium, paraprotein/serum protein electrophoresis, quantitative immunoglobulins, and sFLC at 3 to 6 months to establish stability, then usually annually if stable pending local haematology agreement.
Low-risk MGUS means IgG paraprotein <15 g/L, normal sFLC ratio, no CRAB features, no concerning symptoms, and stable results.
Consider stopping routine surveillance for low-risk MGUS in people over 80 years or with life expectancy under 5 years after shared decision-making and local haematology agreement.
If myeloma tests are normal but symptoms remain unexplained and concerning, repeat baseline tests and safety-net; consider specialist advice or an alternative diagnostic route.

hospital_admission_same_day.text: Suspected myeloma with symptoms/signs of malignant spinal cord compression.
Blood tests or imaging suggestive of myeloma with acute kidney injury.

usoc.text: Raised paraprotein concentration, paraprotein band, abnormal sFLC, or urinary Bence Jones protein plus one or more CRAB features: raised calcium, renal impairment, anaemia, or bone pain.

urgent.text: MGUS with IgG paraprotein >15 g/L, IgA or IgM paraprotein >10 g/L, sFLC ratio outside 0.1 to 7, or paraprotein rise >25% and >5 g/L from baseline.
Any MGUS or paraprotein result with new CRAB symptoms, recurrent infections, neuropathy, suspected AL amyloidosis, or otherwise unexplained clinical deterioration.

routine.text: Raised paraprotein without CRAB features where MGUS risk thresholds are met or monitoring suitability is uncertain.

include_in_referral: Symptoms and duration, especially bone pain, fractures, infection, neuropathy, weight loss, renal symptoms, and MSCC symptoms if present.
FBC, U&E/eGFR, calcium, ESR or plasma viscosity, LFT, serum immunoglobulins, serum protein electrophoresis, sFLC, urine Bence Jones protein if done, and trend over time.
Medication list, relevant comorbidity, frailty, and whether the patient is suitable for investigation or active treatment.

who_not_to_refer.text: Do not refer stable low-risk MGUS as USOC when there are no CRAB features, no concerning symptoms, and no significant laboratory change.
Do not treat MGUS in primary care; it is monitored, not treated.

evidence_notes: NB Medical KISS check is blocked and should be added in a future update pass.
BSH/UKMS full paper PDF extraction was limited; MGUS thresholds should be checked by local D&G haematology before publication.
MGUS monitoring interval differs by source. Draft uses a conservative 3 to 6 month stability check, then annual monitoring if stable pending local agreement.
